Your wiring table's row 'eval.compare, study.compare' puts study.compare under licence::check after pairing::admit, answering 542 and 561. VERBS-study lists 553, 825, 840, 870, 890 on study.compare, neither 542 nor 561. A stored study with a D4 or unrecorded arm read by study.compare is 825 at N37-28's boundary, which runs in the dispatcher before the handler (N37-28's table of paths; N37-REF's and N35-REF's rows as of round 4). Drop study.compare from that row, or state that it calls no licence check, so that no 561 or 542 is raised on a verb whose refusal_lists test forbids them. Your Paths table already gives 825 for the stored study.

The layer-rule note says 'study.compare, eval.compare and the Atelier verbs admit through pairing::admit and answer the twins 553, 555 and 542', but study.compare's row lists only 553 of the three, and the same note gives a stored study's D4 arm to 825.
